BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team
**Re:** Departures from the Buyer Playbook and recommended pushback

## Headline

The Seller's package is framed as "fair and balanced" but, read against our playbook, it departs on almost every protective point. Several departures are not merely commercial but structural: they collapse the Fundamental/Title regime into the general regime, extend the general limitations to *all* claims (including fraud), and replace specific fair disclosure with whole-data-room deemed disclosure. Notably, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter is candid that the three gating items – Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment/assignment – are **not** in the data room. We should not accept the Seller Update as a "negotiated" document; none of these positions have been agreed on our side, and no Amelia Frost authority exists for any fallback.

A preliminary point: the data room cut-off is 22 September 2026, over six weeks ago. We should require a bring-down of the Disclosure Letter and data room index as at signing and again at Completion.

---

## Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1. General Warranty cap (cl 12.1) – 20% / AUD 4.8m
**Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a fallback only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. **None has been given.**
**Analysis:** The Seller presents 20% as if it were an agreed position ("key negotiated positions"). It is not. We have no authority to accept it, and it should not be traded early – it is our principal fallback and should only be offered, if at all, in exchange for movement on Fundamental/Title and fraud carve-outs.
**Push back:** Revert to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not characterise 20% as available.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2) – de minimis AUD 25k / basket AUD 250k / excess-only
**Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
**Analysis:** Three separate departures. The de minimis is 5x ours, the basket 5x ours, and the basket is a deductible (excess-only) rather than a tipping basket. On a AUD 24m deal a AUD 250k deductible with AUD 25k individual threshold could screen out a large proportion of realistic claims (e.g. individual customer/contract issues). The excess-only mechanic is the most damaging of the three.
**Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / tipping basket (liable from first dollar). If forced to concede on quantum, hold the tipping mechanic.

### 3. Time limits (cl 12.3/13) – 18 months, and "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"
**Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
**Analysis:** Two problems. (a) 18 months is unauthorised. (b) The second sentence is a hidden general-regime override: it would sweep Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and covenant claims into the 18-month window unless we remember to carve each one out expressly. This directly contradicts our requirement to keep categories separate and is the kind of drafting that creates traps at the claims stage.
**Push back:** 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default; replace with the opposite default – limitations in cl 12 apply only to general Warranty Claims and do not apply to Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations or covenants except where expressly stated.

### 4. Fundamental / Title – same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity"
**Playbook:** Separate regime; 100% of price cap; minimum six years; outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
**Analysis:** This is the most serious departure. If title to the shares fails, the Buyer's loss is the entire price; capping that at 20% and time-barring it at 18 months is not "administrative simplicity", it is a transfer of the core risk of the deal to us. Title/capacity warranties are the one thing that should be unconditional. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.
**Push back:** Non-negotiable. Separate Fundamental Warranties schedule; cap at 100% of price; 6 years minimum (consider the statutory limitation period for deeds in NSW); excluded from cl 12.2 thresholds and cl 8.3 knowledge bar.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance. No one may waive this.
**Analysis:** "All Claims of any nature" on its face captures fraud. Quite apart from the policy point that a party should not be able to limit its liability for its own fraud, a provision purporting to do so is of doubtful enforceability and signals intent we should not accept. It also catches specific indemnities and payment/covenant claims, which again collapses the categories. The non-reliance clause combined with the proposed knowledge bar (below) would also substantially neuter the warranties as a risk-allocation tool.
**Push back:** Insert an express, overriding fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from every limitation (cap, basket, de minimis, time, exclusive remedy, non-reliance, knowledge), stated to apply "to the maximum extent permitted by law". Confine exclusive remedy and non-reliance to general Warranty Claims only. This is a no-waiver item – no member of the team may trade it.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2) – whole data room and public registers
**Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Analysis:** DL 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in" the data room (DD-002 to DD-012) and 1.2 adds the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". Combined with cl 8.3 this means anything we could have found anywhere is deemed disclosed and deemed known. "Referred to in" is especially broad – it extends to matters merely alluded to in a document. The public-register limb is open-ended (which registers? as at what date?). DL 1.4 (no admission of anything) is standard, but note it means the specific disclosures in sections 2–10 do not concede that any consent, payment or notification is required – so the Seller is simultaneously relying on the disclosures to defeat claims while denying their substance.
**Push back:** Disclosure must be specific, fair and with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter disclosed. Delete 1.1 and 1.2 general disclosure, or at most confine it to documents specifically indexed and listed in an annexure, with the "fairly disclosed" standard applied. Delete public-register deemed disclosure entirely.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) – no claim for any matter known or *discoverable* by Buyer or advisers
**Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
**Analysis:** This is broader than a standard knowledge bar: "discoverable from the data room or public records" imports constructive knowledge, and extending it to "advisers" means the collective knowledge of every lawyer, accountant and consultant we engaged is attributed to us. In practice this makes the warranties close to illusory, because the Seller's defence to any claim becomes "it was in the data room". It is also inconsistent with the purpose of a warranty package, which is to allocate risk for matters the Buyer *cannot* fully verify.
**Push back:** Delete cl 8.3. If a knowledge qualifier is to appear anywhere, it should be on the *Seller's* side (warranties given "so far as the Seller is aware" only where expressly stated, with awareness defined by reference to named individuals after due and careful enquiry). Any residual buyer-knowledge concept must be limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, derived from matters fairly and specifically disclosed, and must never apply to Fundamental/Title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3) – reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery of written consent"
**Playbook:** Effective consent **and** evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.
**Analysis:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue – this is the single largest commercial exposure in the target. DD-002 cl 11.2 requires consent and cl 11.3 attaches conditions. The Seller's formulation satisfies the condition on *delivery* of a document, regardless of whether 11.3 conditions are met, which means we could complete with a conditional consent that lapses. "Reasonable endeavours" is the lowest endeavours standard and would permit the Seller to walk away from the condition if Bluefen proves difficult. The Disclosure Letter confirms **no final consent and no evidence of conditions** is in the data room.
**Push back:** Condition precedent: (i) unconditional written consent from Bluefen in agreed form, or conditional consent plus written evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, (ii) delivered before Completion, (iii) Seller to use all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours, with Buyer right to participate in Bluefen communications, and (iv) Buyer-only waiver right. Consider a long-stop date and a termination right.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7) – ~AUD 3.2m; release "following Completion"
**Playbook:** Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
**Analysis:** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. Accepting a post-completion release means we pay full price, own a company still carrying AUD 3.2m secured debt, and depend on the Seller/bank later discharging it. DD-003 also contains a change-of-control provision (8.1) – Completion without bank consent may itself trigger a default. DL s.3 confirms neither repayment nor discharge is in hand. No Amelia Frost approval exists for a post-completion mechanic.
**Push back:** Pre-Completion payout letter from Riverlark; repayment deducted from and paid directly out of Completion funds under the funds flow; executed deeds of release/discharge and PPSR releases delivered at Completion (held in escrow pending payment); bank's change-of-control consent or waiver obtained. If, as a last resort, a release must follow Completion, require the bank's irrevocable undertaking to release on receipt of the payout amount – and escalate to Amelia Frost before any such concession.

### 10. Funds flow / DD-005 bonuses – AUD 420k "a matter for the Seller", not itemised
**Playbook:** AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Analysis:** The Seller's phrasing is internally inconsistent: if the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller", they should appear as a Seller-funded line item. Leaving them out of the funds flow means the Company (i.e. us, post-Completion) will pay them. The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, so they crystallise as a direct result of our transaction. DL s.5 confirms the disclosure is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs – those are real additional cost (superannuation guarantee may apply depending on characterisation, and NSW payroll tax will). The total could reasonably exceed AUD 500k.
**Push back:** Treat the gross bonus amount plus employer on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, any leave accruals) as a Transaction Expense / Debt-like item deducted from the price and shown as a specific line in the funds flow, or require the Seller to fund them directly with a specific indemnity. Obtain the on-cost calculation from the Seller.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) – indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment
**Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180k not independently verified either way.
**Analysis:** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. If the AUD 180k (per DD-010) is unpaid, the Company may not own the IP in the SOW3 deliverables – a title-to-IP issue, not a payment issue. An indemnity capped at "the SOW3 payment" covers the AUD 180k but not the consequences of non-ownership (loss of IP, third-party claims, re-engineering cost, customer impact). DL s.4 confirms no receipt and no confirmatory assignment in the data room, and notes the AUD 180k figure is not bank-verified.
**Push back:** (i) Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay of all SOW3 Project Materials (this preserves the SOW3 cure); (ii) broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have unrestricted rights to the Ironquay deliverables, not merely the fee; (iii) obtain bank statements to verify whether the AUD 180k is paid. Keep this outside the general cap/basket.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006) – "preliminary, not expected to be material"
**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand.
**Analysis:** The Seller's "not material" is an opinion, not a disclosed fact, and DL s.6 concedes the investigation is preliminary and does not establish access, scope or notification requirement. ~1,240 records of names, business emails, roles and timestamps may engage notifiable data breach obligations depending on what the investigation finds; the material does not currently establish this either way and we should not assert that it does. The risk is that "preliminary" status persists through Completion and the investigation never concludes.
**Push back:** Pre-Completion covenant: preserve all logs and access records; complete the investigation (including link-access/download logs) and report results to Buyer before Completion; comply with any notification obligation determined to apply; warranty bring-down at Completion. Specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident, outside the general regime. Do not demand a price adjustment at this stage – there is no quantified loss.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) – "ordinary-course operating costs"
**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Analysis:** DL s.8 says DD-008 and DD-011 must be "read together for timing/scope" and expressly does not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – so the Seller Update's characterisation goes further than its own disclosure. Three identical AUD 110k renewals from related suppliers warrants a closer look at timing (are they being pulled forward or deferred around Completion?).
**Push back:** Request the underlying documents and the renewal dates/termination rights. Treat as a working-capital/Completion-accounts matter unless the diligence shows an accrued or non-ordinary-course liability, in which case it is a Debt-like item. No automatic deduction.

### 14. Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
**Playbook:** Terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
**Analysis:** Nothing is settled. Folding Tax and IP into the 20%/18-month/AUD 250k-basket regime is inappropriate: tax exposures crystallise on audit, typically beyond 18 months, and IP ownership goes to the value of the business. We have not yet proposed unlimited liability and should not do so, but we should refuse the Seller's characterisation.
**Push back:** Tax warranties/indemnity and IP warranties to be in separate schedules with their own cap and period (to be agreed; standard would be a tax claims period aligned with the ATO amendment periods plus a margin). Record these as open.

### 15. Title – "evidenced by the share register at DD-012"
**Playbook:** Independent evidence required; DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal source.
**Analysis:** The register is maintained by the Company (i.e. by the Seller) and DL s.10 itself notes it merely identifies the source relied on. A register is prima facie, not conclusive, evidence. We need corroboration.
**Push back:** Obtain ASIC company extract and historical extract; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (for security over the shares – note Riverlark may hold share security); original share certificates (or lost-certificate indemnity); board minutes approving issuance and any transfers; Seller board resolution/ constitutional authority to sell; confirmation of no options, convertibles or shareholder agreements. Fundamental Warranties on title, capacity and no encumbrance on the terms in item 4.

### 16. Other matters in the Disclosure Letter
- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation only, per the disclosure. Add as a pre-Completion covenant (Seller to give notice in agreed form) and confirm with the lease text that no consent is required.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** restriction on assignment, not change of control, per the disclosure. Verify the clause ourselves; if correct, no consent needed, but obtain a warranty that no material contract contains a change-of-control right other than Bluefen and Riverlark.
- **DL 1.4 (no admissions):** acceptable in itself, but it should not be allowed to undercut the specific indemnities – the indemnities must operate regardless of whether the Seller admits a consent, payment or notification is required.
- **DL s.11 reservation:** confirms the Buyer must evaluate for itself – which supports our position that nothing in the Seller Update is "agreed".

---

## Summary of recommendations

**Non-negotiable (no team authority to concede):**
1. Fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carved out of every limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provision.
2. Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside thresholds and knowledge bar. Reject "administrative simplicity".
3. Delete the "all limitations apply to all Claims" default and the "all Claims of any nature" language; limitations apply to general Warranty Claims only.

**Revert to playbook (fallbacks require Amelia Frost written authority – none given):**
4. Cap 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal 20% is available.
5. 24-month general claims period.
6. Thresholds AUD 5k / AUD 50k, tipping (first-dollar) basket.

**Delete / replace:**
7. Delete cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion; any qualifier to be Seller-side, named persons, reasonable enquiry; never for title, capacity, fraud, indemnities.
8. Replace general data-room/public-register disclosure with specific fair disclosure.

**Completion mechanics:**
9. Bluefen: effective consent plus evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied, as a CP; all/best endeavours; Buyer-only waiver.
10. Riverlark: payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion, bank CoC consent. Any post-Completion release → irrevocable undertaking + escalate to Amelia Frost.
11. DD-005 bonuses plus on-costs as a specific price-deduction line or Seller-funded with indemnity.
12. Ironquay: payment evidence and confirmatory assignment as Completion deliverables; broadened IP indemnity preserving the SOW3 cure; verify the AUD 180k.
13. Title: independent ASIC/PPSR/certificate/authority evidence.

**Diligence / covenants:**
14. DD-006: preserve logs, complete investigation and report pre-Completion, specific indemnity; no numeric demand.
15. Sandbar: request documents, assess; no automatic deduction.
16. Lease notice and Mossvale verification as pre-Completion steps.
17. Tax and IP: record as OPEN with separate schedules; reject "settled".
18. Require bring-down of the Disclosure Letter and data room (currently dated 22 September 2026) at signing and Completion.

**Process:** Respond with a full mark-up rather than an issues list, so the Seller cannot treat silence on any point as acceptance. Confirm internally that no approval from Amelia Frost exists for any fallback before anyone on the team discusses the cap or claims period with the other side.

If title to the shares fails, the Buyer's loss is the entire price; capping that at 20% and time-barring it at 18 months is not "administrative simplicity", it is a transfer of the core risk of the deal to us. Title/capacity warranties are the one thing that should be unconditional. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.
**Push back:** Non-negotiable. Separate Fundamental Warranties schedule; cap at 100% of price; 6 years minimum (consider the statutory limitation period for deeds in NSW); excluded from cl 12.2 thresholds and cl 8.3 knowledge bar.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance. No one may waive this.
**Analysis:** "All Claims of any nature" on its face captures fraud. Quite apart from the policy point that a party should not be able to limit its liability for its own fraud, a provision purporting to do so is of doubtful enforceability and signals intent we should not accept. It also catches specific indemnities and payment/covenant claims, which again collapses the categories. The non-reliance clause combined with the proposed knowledge bar (below) would also substantially neuter the warranties as a risk-allocation tool.
**Push back:** Insert an express, overriding fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from every limitation (cap, basket, de minimis, time, exclusive remedy, non-reliance, knowledge), stated to apply "to the maximum extent permitted by law". Confine exclusive remedy and non-reliance to general Warranty Claims only. This is a no-waiver item – no member of the team may trade it.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2) – whole data room and public registers
**Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Analysis:** DL 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in" the data room (DD-002 to DD-012) and 1.2 adds the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". Combined with cl 8.3 this means anything we could have found anywhere is deemed disclosed and deemed known. "Referred to in" is especially broad – it extends to matters merely alluded to in a document. The public-register limb is open-ended (which registers? as at what date?). DL 1.4 (no admission of anything) is standard, but note it means the specific disclosures in sections 2–10 do not concede that any consent, payment or notification is required – so the Seller is simultaneously relying on the disclosures to defeat claims while denying their substance.
**Push back:** Disclosure must be specific, fair and with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter disclosed. Delete 1.1 and 1.2 general disclosure, or at most confine it to documents specifically indexed and listed in an annexure, with the "fairly disclosed" standard applied. Delete public-register deemed disclosure entirely.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) – no claim for any matter known or *discoverable* by Buyer or advisers
**Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
**Analysis:** This is broader than a standard knowledge bar: "discoverable from the data room or public records" imports constructive knowledge, and extending it to "advisers" means the collective knowledge of every lawyer, accountant and consultant we engaged is attributed to us. In practice this makes the warranties close to illusory, because the Seller's defence to any claim becomes "it was in the data room". It is also inconsistent with the purpose of a warranty package, which is to allocate risk for matters the Buyer *cannot* fully verify.
**Push back:** Delete cl 8.3. If a knowledge qualifier is to appear anywhere, it should be on the *Seller's* side (warranties given "so far as the Seller is aware" only where expressly stated, with awareness defined by reference to named individuals after due and careful enquiry). Any residual buyer-knowledge concept must be limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, derived from matters fairly and specifically disclosed, and must never apply to Fundamental/Title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3) – reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery of written consent"
**Playbook:** Effective consent **and** evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.
**Analysis:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue – this is the single largest commercial exposure in the target. DD-002 cl 11.2 requires consent and cl 11.3 attaches conditions. The Seller's formulation satisfies the condition on *delivery* of a document, regardless of whether 11.3 conditions are met, which means we could complete with a conditional consent that lapses. "Reasonable endeavours" is the lowest endeavours standard and would permit the Seller to walk away from the condition if Bluefen proves difficult. The Disclosure Letter confirms **no final consent and no evidence of conditions** is in the data room.
**Push back:** Condition precedent: (i) unconditional written consent from Bluefen in agreed form, or conditional consent plus written evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, (ii) delivered before Completion, (iii) Seller to use all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours, with Buyer right to participate in Bluefen communications, and (iv) Buyer-only waiver right. Consider a long-stop date and a termination right.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7) – ~AUD 3.2m; release "following Completion"
**Playbook:** Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
**Analysis:** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. Accepting a post-completion release means we pay full price, own a company still carrying AUD 3.2m secured debt, and depend on the Seller/bank later discharging it. DD-003 also contains a change-of-control provision (8.1) – Completion without bank consent may itself trigger a default. DL s.3 confirms neither repayment nor discharge is in hand. No Amelia Frost approval exists for a post-completion mechanic.
**Push back:** Pre-Completion payout letter from Riverlark; repayment deducted from and paid directly out of Completion funds under the funds flow; executed deeds of release/discharge and PPSR releases delivered at Completion (held in escrow pending payment); bank's change-of-control consent or waiver obtained. If, as a last resort, a release must follow Completion, require the bank's irrevocable undertaking to release on receipt of the payout amount – and escalate to Amelia Frost before any such concession.

### 10. Funds flow / DD-005 bonuses – AUD 420k "a matter for the Seller", not itemised
**Playbook:** AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Analysis:** The Seller's phrasing is internally inconsistent: if the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller", they should appear as a Seller-funded line item. Leaving them out of the funds flow means the Company (i.e. us, post-Completion) will pay them. The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, so they crystallise as a direct result of our transaction. DL s.5 confirms the disclosure is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs – those are real additional cost (superannuation guarantee may apply depending on characterisation, and NSW payroll tax will). The total could reasonably exceed AUD 500k.
**Push back:** Treat the gross bonus amount plus employer on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, any leave accruals) as a Transaction Expense / Debt-like item deducted from the price and shown as a specific line in the funds flow, or require the Seller to fund them directly with a specific indemnity. Obtain the on-cost calculation from the Seller.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) – indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment
**Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180k not independently verified either way.
**Analysis:** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. If the AUD 180k (per DD-010) is unpaid, the Company may not own the IP in the SOW3 deliverables – a title-to-IP issue, not a payment issue. An indemnity capped at "the SOW3 payment" covers the AUD 180k but not the consequences of non-ownership (loss of IP, third-party claims, re-engineering cost, customer impact). DL s.4 confirms no receipt and no confirmatory assignment in the data room, and notes the AUD 180k figure is not bank-verified.
**Push back:** (i) Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay of all SOW3 Project Materials (this preserves the SOW3 cure); (ii) broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have unrestricted rights to the Ironquay deliverables, not merely the fee; (iii) obtain bank statements to verify whether the AUD 180k is paid. Keep this outside the general cap/basket.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006) – "preliminary, not expected to be material"
**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand.
**Analysis:** The Seller's "not material" is an opinion, not a disclosed fact, and DL s.6 concedes the investigation is preliminary and does not establish access, scope or notification requirement. ~1,240 records of names, business emails, roles and timestamps may engage notifiable data breach obligations depending on what the investigation finds; the material does not currently establish this either way and we should not assert that it does. The risk is that "preliminary" status persists through Completion and the investigation never concludes.
**Push back:** Pre-Completion covenant: preserve all logs and access records; complete the investigation (including link-access/download logs) and report results to Buyer before Completion; comply with any notification obligation determined to apply; warranty bring-down at Completion. Specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident, outside the general regime. Do not demand a price adjustment at this stage – there is no quantified loss.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) – "ordinary-course operating costs"
**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Analysis:** DL s.8 says DD-008 and DD-011 must be "read together for timing/scope" and expressly does not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – so the Seller Update's characterisation goes further than its own disclosure. Three identical AUD 110k renewals from related suppliers warrants a closer look at timing (are they being pulled forward or deferred around Completion?).
**Push back:** Request the underlying documents and the renewal dates/termination rights. Treat as a working-capital/Completion-accounts matter unless the diligence shows an accrued or non-ordinary-course liability, in which case it is a Debt-like item. No automatic deduction.

### 14. Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
**Playbook:** Terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
**Analysis:** Nothing is settled. Folding Tax and IP into the 20%/18-month/AUD 250k-basket regime is inappropriate: tax exposures crystallise on audit, typically beyond 18 months, and IP ownership goes to the value of the business. We have not yet proposed unlimited liability and should not do so, but we should refuse the Seller's characterisation.
**Push back:** Tax warranties/indemnity and IP warranties to be in separate schedules with their own cap and period (to be agreed; standard would be a tax claims period aligned with the ATO amendment periods plus a margin). Record these as open.

### 15. Title – "evidenced by the share register at DD-012"
**Playbook:** Independent evidence required; DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal source.
**Analysis:** The register is maintained by the Company (i.e. by the Seller) and DL s.10 itself notes it merely identifies the source relied on. A register is prima facie, not conclusive, evidence. We need corroboration.
**Push back:** Obtain ASIC company extract and historical extract; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (for security over the shares – note Riverlark may hold share security); original share certificates (or lost-certificate indemnity); board minutes approving issuance and any transfers; Seller board resolution/ constitutional authority to sell; confirmation of no options, convertibles or shareholder agreements. Fundamental Warranties on title, capacity and no encumbrance on the terms in item 4.

### 16. Other matters in the Disclosure Letter
- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation only, per the disclosure. Add as a pre-Completion covenant (Seller to give notice in agreed form) and confirm with the lease text that no consent is required.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** restriction on assignment, not change of control, per the disclosure. Verify the clause ourselves; if correct, no consent needed, but obtain a warranty that no material contract contains a change-of-control right other than Bluefen and Riverlark.
- **DL 1.4 (no admissions):** acceptable in itself, but it should not be allowed to undercut the specific indemnities – the indemnities must operate regardless of whether the Seller admits a consent, payment or notification is required.
- **DL s.11 reservation:** confirms the Buyer must evaluate for itself – which supports our position that nothing in the Seller Update is "agreed".

## Summary of recommendations

**Non-negotiable (no team authority to concede):**
1. Fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carved out of every limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provision.
2. Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside thresholds and knowledge bar. Reject "administrative simplicity".
3. Delete the "all limitations apply to all Claims" default and the "all Claims of any nature" language; limitations apply to general Warranty Claims only.

**Revert to playbook (fallbacks require Amelia Frost written authority – none given):**
4. Cap 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal 20% is available.
5. 24-month general claims period.
6. Thresholds AUD 5k / AUD 50k, tipping (first-dollar) basket.

**Delete / replace:**
7. Delete cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion; any qualifier to be Seller-side, named persons, reasonable enquiry; never for title, capacity, fraud, indemnities.
8. Replace general data-room/public-register disclosure with specific fair disclosure.

**Completion mechanics:**
9. Bluefen: effective consent plus evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied, as a CP; all/best endeavours; Buyer-only waiver.
10. Riverlark: payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion, bank CoC consent. Any post-Completion release → irrevocable undertaking + escalate to Amelia Frost.
11. DD-005 bonuses plus on-costs as a specific price-deduction line or Seller-funded with indemnity.
12. Ironquay: payment evidence and confirmatory assignment as Completion deliverables; broadened IP indemnity preserving the SOW3 cure; verify the AUD 180k.
13. Title: independent ASIC/PPSR/certificate/authority evidence.

**Diligence / covenants:**
14. DD-006: preserve logs, complete investigation and report pre-Completion, specific indemnity; no numeric demand.
15. Sandbar: request documents, assess; no automatic deduction.
16. Lease notice and Mossvale verification as pre-Completion steps.
17. Tax and IP: record as OPEN with separate schedules; reject "settled".
18. Require bring-down of the Disclosure Letter and data room (currently dated 22 September 2026) at signing and Completion.

**Process:** Respond with a full mark-up rather than an issues list, so the Seller cannot treat silence on any point as acceptance. Confirm internally that no approval from Amelia Frost exists for any fallback before anyone on the team discusses the cap or claims period with the other side.
